{"notes":"RESULTS 2026-11-13: coland deployed at https://coland.reviewcommit.com (instance i-0c081557a03171f75, 172.31.42.108).

BUILD (on the dev box, release, CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/data/cargo/coland-target, rustc 1.100.0; workspace rust-version 1.99, no rust-toolchain.toml)
- coland 76ef1bf5ea070ddfb5d8cdaf49e1a8ba14086e69 (main, 2026-11-14 02:40 +0800), version 0.3.0.
- Sibling path deps at HEAD. coland's .ci/release-sources.json pins are stale for main, and building with them fails in coland-storage-postgres. The HEADs used: arkret-rust-sdk 073b4317a644, arkret-spec a4942f743b75, floria 19d244b9b00d, garth 869b87fd8d13, bridges 9e8075e93620.
- Binaries /usr/local/bin/coland (sha256 2531e9bf...497d) and coland-keystore-keygen (1df40e20...6d73).

DEPLOYMENT
- Caddy 2.6.2 (Debian) on :80/:443 with automatic Let's Encrypt (cert obtained 21:01Z, tls-alpn-01), reverse_proxy to 127.0.0.1:8698. Config /etc/caddy/Caddyfile, access log /var/log/caddy/coland-access.log.
- TLS choice: Caddy terminates; coland serves plaintext on loopback. Reasons: (1) coland authenticates MIMI peers by RFC 9421 HTTP signatures, not TLS client certs, so terminating at the proxy loses nothing, and coland derives @target-uri from COLAND_PUBLIC_BASE_URL plus X-Forwarded-Host, which is designed for exactly this setup. (2) coland's own rustls listener also accepts classical TLS, so it would fail coland's PQ probe anyway (.7). (3) A PQ-only endpoint would lock out the OpenSSL 3.0 peers mimid uses. COLAND_PQ_TLS_DEPLOYMENT_PROBE=unverified-classical-caddy skips the self-probe, so /readyz is honestly 503 pq_hybrid_tls_probe_missing. /health is 200, and every route serves normally.
- coland: systemd unit /etc/systemd/system/coland.service, User=coland (system), EnvironmentFile=/etc/coland/coland.env (root:coland 0640), ProtectSystem=strict, ReadWritePaths=/var/lib/coland, NoNewPrivileges, PrivateTmp/Devices, empty CapabilityBoundingSet, SystemCallFilter=@system-service minus privileged subsets except @chown (the keystore needs fchown; ~@privileged killed it with SIGSYS).
- Listeners: 127.0.0.1:8698 (HTTP API), 127.0.0.1:9698 (Prometheus /metrics). No new public port is needed.
- DB: PostgreSQL 15.20 (Debian), role/db coland, scram password in /etc/coland/secrets/db-password (root 0600) and in DATABASE_URL. Migrations applied at boot. Upstream recommends PG 16+, but 15 worked.
- KeyStore: COLAND_KEYSTORE_BACKEND=encrypted_file, ciphertext /var/lib/coland/keystore/coland.v1. The master key was generated by coland-keystore-keygen and is kept at /etc/coland/secrets/keystore-master-key (root 0400). It is passed via systemd LoadCredential to /run/credentials/coland.service/keystore-master-key and is not in the env file.
- Identity: first boot ran with COLAND_FIRST_PROVISIONING=true (now commented out). Service DID: did:webvh:Qmbt1KN87RzzrzXEvtceNq35pfvcDtaDBGW7zBs5MiQqux:coland.reviewcommit.com:webvh:service, core id ak:did_core:webvh:Qmbt1KN87RzzrzXEvtceNq35pfvcDtaDBGW7zBs5MiQqux. The identity bundle is in /var/lib/coland/identity-bundle. The embedded webvh provider is on only so the DID log is served at /webvh/service/did.jsonl. Its registration bearer is random (in the env file and /etc/coland/secrets/webvh-registration-bearer) and held by no one, so registration is closed.
- Other env: COLAND_BIND=127.0.0.1:8698, COLAND_METRICS_BIND=127.0.0.1:9698, COLAND_PUBLIC_BASE_URL=https://coland.reviewcommit.com, COLAND_TRUST_DOMAIN=ak:trust_domain:coland.reviewcommit.com, COLAND_SERVICE_IDENTITY_BUNDLE_DIR, COLAND_OBJECT_STORAGE_BACKEND=filesystem (/var/lib/coland/objects), COLAND_RESUMABLE_UPLOAD_DIR, COLAND_RATE_LIMIT_TRUST_X_FORWARDED_FOR=true, COLAND_SHUTDOWN_GRACE_SECS=20, RUST_LOG=coland=info,salvo=info,warn. Development mode is off. There is no Account Authority (coauth), so the admin API is closed and no users or devices can be created.
- The MIMI facade is always on (ak.profile.mimi_interop.v1); no flag is needed.

OPERATE
- Restart: sudo systemctl restart coland. Status: systemctl status coland caddy.
- Logs: sudo journalctl -u coland -f (JSON lines); sudo journalctl -u caddy; /var/log/caddy/coland-access.log.
- Health: curl https://coland.reviewcommit.com/health (and /readyz, which is expected to be 503).
- Upgrade: rebuild on the dev box, scp, sudo install -m0755 to /usr/local/bin, restart. Keep the DB, keystore, master key and identity-bundle together.

SMOKE (from the dev box)
- GET /.well-known/mimi-protocol-directory returns 200 with an Arkret ProviderDirectory, and is identical to GET /_arkret/open/mimi/provider-directory (which needs an Arkret-Operation header). The directory declares protocol-06 and provider_id mimi://coland.reviewcommit.com/webvh/service. Six endpoints are listed: consent, identifier_query, key_material, notify, room_update, submit_message. Nothing matches the -06/-07 §5.1 keys (.1).
- mimid-seed-probe (mimid PeerClient, -07 keyMaterial for mimi://coland.reviewcommit.com/u/alice): FAIL, "the peer does not offer keyMaterial" (.1).
- POST /v1/keyMaterial/... gives 404. An unsigned POST to the facade key-material or identifiers/query gives 401 http_signature_required (.2, .3).
- A did:key-signed identifiers/query via arkret-http-client (probe in scratchpad coland/probe) gives 200 {"matches":[{..,"matched":false}],"has_more":false}. This proves the signature path and shows any DID-keyed source is accepted (.2, .5).
- keyMaterial was not attempted: it is native-Arkret-only and no user can be seeded without coauth (.4).

PEER AUTH / WHAT mimid NEEDS
coland does no mTLS and has no CA list, so the mimid interop CA was not copied. To be accepted, mimid would need: (a) a DID with an Ed25519 key (did:key works offline; did:web:mimid.reviewcommit.com would need /.well-known/did.json); (b) RFC 9421 signing per scenario mimi_provider.v1 (.2); (c) Arkret JSON bodies plus the Arkret-Operation header on /_arkret/open/mimi/* (.3). Even with all of that, keyMaterial stays closed to non-Arkret providers (.4), and identifierQuery never matches (.5). So no mimid-box wiring would make a -07 exchange succeed. The peer base URL would be https://coland.reviewcommit.com (directory at /.well-known/mimi-protocol-directory), port 443 only, with no client credential to provision.

FINDINGS: .1 directory format; .2 auth (sigs, not mTLS); .3 wire (JSON, not TLS-PL); .4 keyMaterial native-only; .5 identifierQuery stub; .6 provider_id path; .7 PQ probe; .8 draft: no version in the directory."}
